corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from the author's own run (the README table was added 2024-04-10). The committed code does not exactly reproduce the table. SyncBenchmarks.cs declares [Params(1_000_000)] iterations but does one round-trip per invocation, and its Test class has no string field. SyncBenchmarksWithStrings.cs loops 1M times, but it uses an 18-field class and has no iterations parameter. The exact class that produced the table cannot be identified. 'Protobuf' is protobuf-net 3.1.26, not Google.Protobuf, although the README links protocolbuffers/protobuf. The '16x' figure (2024 text table) and the '18x' / '3x vs Apex' figures (2022 PNG chart with no environment) come from different runs. The format is contract-less and positional: it has no schema evolution, and dictionaries and complex-type properties are not serialized. The repo LICENSE is Apache-2.0, but the NuGet package ships License.txt with MIT text. Both licenses are OSI-approved.

tier_reason: The paper is a single-author arXiv preprint (cs.SE, v1 of 4 Jan 2026) with no journal reference, so it is not peer-reviewed. Table I gives byte sizes against MessagePack, but there is no code, hardware or implementation detail, so the evidence is first-party numbers with thin methodology.

corrections.caveats: No code repository or specification is published. The only reproducibility aid is the author's email. This is a January 2026 single-author arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed) with synthetic datasets only (10k/20k/50k payloads generated from Magenta metric samples). The win over MessagePack is modest: 1,390,000 vs 1,469,521 bytes on S1 (5.4%). The MTS-1 sizes are exactly 139 B per payload on every dataset (1,390,000 / 2,780,000 / 6,950,000 bytes), which suggests computed rather than measured values. MTS-1+LZ4 is larger than plain MTS-1. MTS-1 drops changes below a threshold epsilon, so it is lossy by design, although the paper claims identical semantic information. The abstract says encoding cost was compared, but no encoding-time results are reported. Protocol Buffers was excluded from the quantitative tests.

notes: The numbers match Table I and the abstract (74.6% vs JSON on S1, 74.7% on S2, 5.4% vs MessagePack). A web search and a GitHub search found no implementation. A related Medium post returned 403 and was not read. This stays a paper-only research entry at tier C.
